exam_set.title: Practice Set 3
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 10, Practice Set 3

questions.jp: IPv6のIPアドレスは何ビットか。
questions.romaji: IPv6 no IP adoresu wa nan-bitto ka.
questions.en: How many bits are in an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
IPv6 uses a much larger address box: 128 bits.

Technical breakdown:
The IPv6 standard defines an address as 128 bits, commonly written as eight 16-bit hexadecimal groups separated by colons. IPv4 uses 32 bits.

Japanese keywords to remember:
IPアドレス = IP adoresu = IP address
何ビット = nan-bitto = how many bits

Why the best solution works:
ウ states the defined IPv6 address length of 128 bits.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
32 bits is IPv4's address length.
イ:
64 bits commonly appears as an IPv6 interface-ID or subnet-prefix length, not the whole address.
エ:
IPv6 addresses are not 256 bits.

Memory trick:
IPv4 = 32; IPv6 = 128.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: IPv6アドレスの特徴として、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: IPv6 adoresu no tokuchō to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which statement correctly describes an IPv6 address?

options.label: ア
options.jp: アドレス長は96ビットである。
options.romaji: Adoresu-chō wa 96 bitto de aru.
options.en: Its address length is 96 bits.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 全てグローバルアドレスである。
options.romaji: Subete gurōbaru adoresu de aru.
options.en: All are global addresses.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 全てのIPv6アドレスとIPv4アドレスを、1対1に対応付けることができる。
options.romaji: Subete no IPv6 adoresu to IPv4 adoresu o, ittai-ichi ni taiōzukeru koto ga dekiru.
options.en: Every IPv6 address can be mapped one-to-one to an IPv4 address.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 複数のアドレス表記法があり、その一つは、アドレスの16進数表記を4文字（16ビット）ずつコロン“:”で区切る方法である。
options.romaji: Fukusū no adoresu hyōkihō ga ari, sono hitotsu wa, adoresu no 16-shinsū hyōki o 4-moji (16 bitto) zutsu koron ':' de kugiru hōhō de aru.
options.en: There are multiple address notations; one separates hexadecimal notation into four-character (16-bit) groups with colons (:).

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
IPv6 is usually written as groups of four hexadecimal digits separated by colons.

Technical breakdown:
A full IPv6 address has eight 16-bit groups, each represented by up to four hexadecimal digits, separated with colons. Compression rules can omit leading zeros and one run of zero groups, so multiple notations exist.

Japanese keywords to remember:
16進数表記 = jūroku-shinsū hyōki = hexadecimal notation
区切る = kugiru = separate

Why the best solution works:
エ accurately describes a standard IPv6 textual form and acknowledges compressed alternatives.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
IPv6 length is 128 bits, not 96.
イ:
IPv6 includes link-local, unique-local, multicast, and other non-global addresses.
ウ:
IPv6's vastly larger space prevents universal one-to-one mapping with IPv4.

Memory trick:
IPv6: hex groups joined by colons.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: TCP/IPネットワークにおいて、IPアドレスを動的に割り当てるプロトコルはどれか。
questions.romaji: TCP/IP nettowāku ni oite, IP adoresu o dōteki ni wariateru purotokoru wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which protocol dynamically assigns IP addresses in a TCP/IP network?

options.label: ア
options.jp: ARP
options.romaji: ARP
options.en: ARP

options.label: イ
options.jp: DHCP
options.romaji: DHCP
options.en: DHCP

options.label: ウ
options.jp: RIP
options.romaji: RIP
options.en: RIP

options.label: エ
options.jp: SMTP
options.romaji: SMTP
options.en: SMTP

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
DHCP automatically lends a device its network settings when it joins.

Technical breakdown:
Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol supplies clients with leased IP addresses and commonly subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS server information.

Japanese keywords to remember:
動的に = dōteki ni = dynamically
割り当てる = wariateru = assign

Why the best solution works:
イ is the TCP/IP configuration protocol designed for dynamic address allocation.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
ARP resolves an IPv4 address to a link-layer address.
ウ:
RIP exchanges routing information.
エ:
SMTP transfers electronic mail.

Memory trick:
DHCP = Dynamic Host Configuration.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: IPv4において、インターネット接続用ルーターのNAT機能の説明として、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: IPv4 ni oite, intānetto setsuzoku-yō rūta no NAT kinō no setsumei to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: In IPv4, which correctly describes the NAT function of an Internet access router?

options.label: ア
options.jp: インターネットへのアクセスをキャッシュしておくことによって、その後に同じIPアドレスのWebサイトへアクセスする場合、表示を高速化できる機能である。
options.romaji: Intānetto e no akusesu o kyasshu shite oku koto ni yotte, sono ato ni onaji IP adoresu no Web saito e akusesu suru baai, hyōji o kōsokuka dekiru kinō de aru.
options.en: It caches Internet access to speed later access to a website at the same IP address.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 通信中のIPパケットを検査して、インターネットからの攻撃や侵入を検知する機能である。
options.romaji: Tsūshin-chū no IP paketto o kensa shite, intānetto kara no kōgeki ya shinnyū o kenchi suru kinō de aru.
options.en: It inspects IP packets to detect attacks and intrusions from the Internet.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 特定の端末宛てのIPパケットだけを通過させる機能である。
options.romaji: Tokutei no tanmatsu-ate no IP paketto dake o tsūka saseru kinō de aru.
options.en: It passes only IP packets addressed to a particular terminal.

options.label: エ
options.jp: プライベートIPアドレスとグローバルIPアドレスを相互に変換する機能である。
options.romaji: Puraibēto IP adoresu to gurōbaru IP adoresu o sōgo ni henkan suru kinō de aru.
options.en: It translates between private and global IP addresses.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
NAT rewrites inside private addresses into outside global addresses and back.

Technical breakdown:
Network Address Translation changes address fields as packets cross a boundary, mapping private IPv4 addresses to global IPv4 addresses and translating return traffic using maintained mapping state.

Japanese keywords to remember:
相互に変換 = sōgo ni henkan = translate mutually
プライベートIPアドレス = puraibēto IP adoresu = private IP address

Why the best solution works:
エ states NAT's defining address-translation function.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
This describes Web caching or a proxy cache.
イ:
This describes intrusion detection or firewall inspection.
ウ:
This describes packet filtering, not address translation.

Memory trick:
NAT = Network Address Translation.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: プライベートIPアドレスをもつ複数の端末が、一つのグローバルIPアドレスを使ってインターネット接続を利用する仕組みを実現するものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Puraibēto IP adoresu o motsu fukusū no tanmatsu ga, hitotsu no gurōbaru IP adoresu o tsukatte intānetto setsuzoku o riyō suru shikumi o jitsugen suru mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which mechanism lets multiple private-IP devices access the Internet using one global IP address?

options.label: ア
options.jp: DHCP
options.romaji: DHCP
options.en: DHCP

options.label: イ
options.jp: DNS
options.romaji: DNS
options.en: DNS

options.label: ウ
options.jp: NAPT
options.romaji: NAPT
options.en: NAPT

options.label: エ
options.jp: RADIUS
options.romaji: RADIUS
options.en: RADIUS

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
NAPT distinguishes many inside devices by rewriting both address and port, so one public address can be shared.

Technical breakdown:
Network Address Port Translation maps private address-and-port pairs to one global address with different port numbers. Return packets are demultiplexed through that translation table.

Japanese keywords to remember:
複数の端末 = fukusū no tanmatsu = multiple devices
一つのグローバルIPアドレス = hitotsu no gurōbaru IP adoresu = one global IP address

Why the best solution works:
ウ enables many simultaneous sessions to share one global IPv4 address through port translation.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
DHCP allocates network configuration; it does not share a global address.
イ:
DNS maps names and IP addresses.
エ:
RADIUS supplies centralized authentication, authorization, and accounting.

Memory trick:
NAPT adds Port to NAT.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: TCP/IPネットワークでDNSが果たす役割はどれか。
questions.romaji: TCP/IP nettowāku de DNS ga hatasu yakuwari wa dore ka.
questions.en: What role does DNS perform in a TCP/IP network?

options.label: ア
options.jp: PCやプリンターなどからのIPアドレス付与の要求に対して、サーバに登録してあるIPアドレスの中から使用されていないIPアドレスを割り当てる。
options.romaji: PC ya purintā nado kara no IP adoresu fuyo no yōkyū ni taishite, sāba ni tōroku shite aru IP adoresu no naka kara shiyō sarete inai IP adoresu o wariateru.
options.en: Assign an unused registered IP address when a PC or printer requests one.

options.label: イ
options.jp: サーバにあるプログラムを、サーバのIPアドレスを意識することなく、プログラム名の指定だけで呼び出すようにする。
options.romaji: Sāba ni aru puroguramu o, sāba no IP adoresu o ishiki suru koto naku, puroguramu-mei no shitei dake de yobidasu yō ni suru.
options.en: Invoke a server program by program name without considering the server IP address.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 社内のプライベートIPアドレスをグローバルIPアドレスに変換し、インターネットへのアクセスを可能にする。
options.romaji: Shanai no puraibēto IP adoresu o gurōbaru IP adoresu ni henkan shi, intānetto e no akusesu o kanō ni suru.
options.en: Translate an internal private IP address into a global IP address for Internet access.

options.label: エ
options.jp: ドメイン名やホスト名などとIPアドレスとを対応付ける。
options.romaji: Domein-mei ya hosuto-mei nado to IP adoresu to o taiōzukeru.
options.en: Associate domain or host names with IP addresses.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
DNS is the Internet's address book: names in, IP addresses out.

Technical breakdown:
The Domain Name System is a distributed hierarchical naming service. Resource records associate domain/host names with IP addresses and other information, enabling name resolution.

Japanese keywords to remember:
ドメイン名 = domein-mei = domain name
対応付ける = taiōzukeru = associate/map

Why the best solution works:
エ describes DNS name-to-address association.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Dynamic allocation of unused IP addresses is DHCP.
イ:
Program-by-name invocation is not DNS's defined role.
ウ:
Private-to-global address translation is NAT.

Memory trick:
DNS: domain name ↔ IP.

Correct answer: エ
